statement: For iid continuous labels U_z on Z^d, let a(x) be the minimum-label site in x+[-L,L]^d and X_x=1 iff a(y)=a(x) for x and every nearest neighbour y. The field is (2L+2)-dependent in sup norm, P(X_x=1)=(2L-1)^d/[(2L+1)^(d-1)(2L+1+2d)] tends to 1 as L grows, and every nearest-neighbour good component has at most (2L+1)^d sites.
source: owner-own-work: w429 ATTEMPT.md L1, independently reproduced in w431 REVIEW_PACKET.md
proof_or_counterexample: The common anchor is the unique minimum on the union of the 2d+1 windows iff it lies in their intersection; intersection size (2L-1)^d, union size (2L+1)^d+2d(2L+1)^(d-1). Label support lies within distance L+1, giving dependence range 2L+2. Adjacent good vertices share their anchor, trapping a component in a translate of [-L,L]^d.
remaining_gap: This field is not asserted to be FKG or monotone in Bernoulli bonds; it does not settle C0023.

statement: In nearest-neighbour Bernoulli bond percolation on Z^d, d>=2, P_{p_c}(0 connects to the vertex boundary of [-n,n]^d)>=1/[2d p_c(2n+1)^(d-1)] for n>=1. Thus a subcritical exponential one-arm estimate with constants uniform as p increases to p_c is impossible.
assumptions: Duminil-Copin--Tassion 2015 Theorem 1.1: tilde p_c=p_c for the finite-set phi criterion
source: https://arxiv.org/html/1502.03051v1 Theorem 1.1 and (1.1)-(1.2); owner-own-work: w430 ATTEMPT.md
proof_or_counterexample: For every finite S containing 0, phi_{p_c}(S)>=1, else finite-event continuity extends phi<1 above p_c. For S=[-n,n]^d, its 2d(2n+1)^(d-1) boundary edges have inside endpoints on the vertex boundary; each summand is at most the one-arm probability. Hence 1<=p_c*2d(2n+1)^(d-1)*a_n(p_c). A uniform exponential estimate below p_c would pass to p_c by finite-event continuity and contradict this polynomial lower bound.
remaining_gap: This lower bound gives no upper decay at p_c and does not settle C0023.

statement: Theorem 1.1 of Duminil-Copin--Tassion 2015 gives, for each fixed p<p_c in nearest-neighbour Bernoulli bond percolation on Z^d, some c(p)>0 with P_p(0 connects to distance n)<=exp(-c(p)n) for all n>=1; it does not assert inf_{p<p_c}c(p)>0 or theta(p_c)=0.
proof_or_counterexample: The source explicitly quantifies c=c(p). R02 independently contradicts any uniform positive exponential rate near p_c.
remaining_gap: A valid upper critical one-arm decay estimate is still needed if this route is used.

statement: Let X be a {0,1} field on Z^d, d>=2, with setwise sigma-field independence for vertex sets at infinity-norm distance greater than integer r>=0. If every bad marginal is at most 64^(-4)/(r+1)^2, then the origin lies in an infinite nearest-neighbour good component with positive probability.
source: owner-own-work: w430 REVIEW_PACKET.md claim 003; w429 L2 fixed-range contour lemma
proof_or_counterexample: Set s=r+1 and tile a coordinate plane into s by s squares. At coarse separation greater than one, tile unions have physical separation at least s+1>r, hence the all-good tile field is setwise 1-dependent. Its bad marginal is at most s^2 delta<=64^-4. The independently checked r=1 contour lemma yields an infinite good-tile path with positive probability. Every tile on it is fully good and adjacent tiles connect by nearest-neighbour edges, including the origin in the origin tile.
remaining_gap: No derivation of compatible finite critical blocks with this bad-marginal threshold; C0023 remains unresolved within this route.

statement: For independent Bernoulli bond percolation on Z^d with d>=2 and independent green vertices of density 1-exp(-h), put m_h(p)=P_{p,h}(C(0) meets green). At p=p_c, q_h=p_c(1-m_h(p_c)) increases to p_c(1-theta(p_c)) as h decreases to zero. Thus q_h tends to p_c iff theta(p_c)=0; Theorem 2 of arXiv:2304.12110 compares cluster-volume tails at q_h and p_c and alone cannot establish this endpoint.
assumptions: Green marks independent of bonds and each other
Infinite clusters meet green almost surely
source: https://arxiv.org/html/2304.12110 Theorem 2 and magnetization definition; owner-own-work: w430 claim 004
proof_or_counterexample: Given cluster size k, the no-green probability is exp(-hk), with exp(-h infinity)=0. Hence m_h(p)=E_p[1-exp(-h|C(0)|)]>=theta(p), and bounded convergence gives m_h(p)->theta(p) as h decreases to zero. Multiply by p_c>0. Theorem 2's parameter q=p(1-m_h(p)) is therefore uniformly below p_c by at least p_c theta(p_c) under hypothetical theta(p_c)>0.
remaining_gap: No critical upper volume-tail bound; the exponential factor exp(-hn) vanishes as a useful rate when h decreases to zero.

statement: The live Burton-Keane card's strict finite-energy hypothesis is satisfied by independent Bernoulli(p) bonds precisely when 0<p<1; the card's sentence claiming all three hypotheses for every p has false endpoint applications.
assumptions: Finite energy is defined by a.s. conditional edge-open probabilities strictly between 0 and 1
source: Read-only live math-brain card claim_19571635c9811ef2c4fa9bf7413abff7ada34807a8dc3b1fc48636004a01b663; owner-own-work: w429 C1
proof_or_counterexample: Independence makes P(omega_e=1 | all other edges)=p a.s., which is strictly between zero and one exactly for 0<p<1. This corrects theorem applicability, not its separate endpoint conclusions.
remaining_gap: A separate source-statement reviewer should approve any edit to the live theorem card; no store edit was made.
